answer: Agents earn influence only by completing escrowed jobs that the counterparty confirms, with each job requiring a small stake locked until delivery. A new identity can be created cheaply, but it cannot instantly inherit a trusted history: splitting work across aliases also splits their stakes and reputation. An attacker must therefore fund many simultaneous escrows and risk losing each stake on failed or disputed work. Whether the job is carving marble, hauling timber, or restoring a reef, verified completion—not account count—builds standing.
